title: Accessible Days Out: Carer Tickets, Passes and Tips
description: Accessible family days out: carer tickets, Max Card and CEA Card discounts, ride access passes, quiet sessions, Changing Places toilets and how to plan ahead.
h1: Accessible days out: tips for disabled children and families
intro: Every family deserves a great day out. These schemes and tips help families with disabled children or additional needs plan with confidence.

image.alt: Two parents holding a toddler’s hands on a sunny walk

cardText: Carer tickets, Max Card, CEA Card and ride access passes.

blocks.title: Scout’s access tip
blocks.text: Check the attraction’s accessibility page and contact them before you go. Many offer free carer tickets, quiet times and access passes, but you may need to apply in advance.
points: Bring any proof of eligibility they ask for
Ask about quiet rooms and sensory maps

sections.html:
• Carer tickets: many attractions offer free or discounted entry for an essential carer.
  • Max Card: a discount card for families of children with additional needs, accepted at participating attractions.
  • CEA Card: lets a cardholder get a free ticket for a carer at participating cinemas.
Merlin parks use the Ride Access Pass, which you apply for online in advance. Disney has its own access services. Read our queue tips and check each park’s accessibility pages.

Look for relaxed or SEN-friendly sessions at cinemas, trampoline parks and museums, plus sensory maps and quiet rooms. Changing Places toilets (with a hoist and changing bench) are listed online. Use the adventure finder to plan.

faqs.q: Do carers get free entry to attractions?
faqs.a: Many UK attractions offer free or discounted entry for an essential carer, sometimes with proof of eligibility. Check the attraction’s accessibility page.
